title: Assent without legitimate object-ground is blind obstinacy, not true certainty
source_text: IV. Caeterum illa certitudo, quae menti quidem inest, nullum tamen in objecto legitimum fundamentum habet, veri nominis certitudo non est, sed potius obstinata & caeca persuasio.
pass_a_gloss: But that certainty which indeed is in the mind, yet has no legitimate foundation in the object, is not certainty of the true name, but rather obstinate and blind persuasion.
pass_b_english: Mind-internal ‘certainty’ without legitimate object-ground ≠ true certitudo.
Name it obstinate, blind persuasio instead.

lemmas.gloss: is not certainty of the true name

choices.why: Strips false certainty of the name.
rejected: any firm mental cling counts as true certainty
